root_cause.text: F2FS performs partial directory modifications (updating target entry and deleting source entry) before attempting to add the whiteout entry via f2fs_add_link, but when f2fs_add_link fails, the VFS dentry cache is not invalidated, leaving stale mappings that point to inodes with already-decremented i_nlink values.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds explicit d_invalidate() calls for both old_dentry and new_dentry in the error path of f2fs_add_link during RENAME_WHITEOUT operations. The CVE description explicitly states: "VFS assumes the entire rename operation failed and does not update the dentry cache, leaving stale mappings" and "In the error path, VFS does not call d_move() to update the dentry cache. This results in new_dentry still pointing to the old inode (new_inode) which has already had its i_nlink decremented to zero." The fix forces VFS to refresh from disk by invalidating the cached dentries when the whiteout creation fails, preventing subsequent operations from using stale inode references.

intent_record.intent_summary: Invalidate stale dentries on whiteout link addition failure to prevent dcache inconsistency during rename operations.
intent_record.what: Added two d_invalidate() calls within the error handling block of the whiteout link addition. When f2fs_add_link() fails, the code now invalidates both old_dentry and new_dentry before jumping to put_out_dir label. Also reformatted the if-statement braces to multi-line style.
intent_record.how: When adding a whiteout link fails, the dentries (directory entries) for both the old and new paths are now explicitly invalidated, which removes them from the dcache and marks them as invalid. This prevents stale dentry references from persisting in the kernel's directory cache after a failed rename operation with whiteout, ensuring subsequent operations see consistent filesystem state.

commit 7e01e7ad746bc8198a8b46163ddc73a1c7d22339
Author: Chao Yu <chao@kernel.org>
Date:   Tue May 19 17:37:26 2015 +0800

    f2fs: support RENAME_WHITEOUT
    
    As the description of rename in manual, RENAME_WHITEOUT is a special operation
    that only makes sense for overlay/union type filesystem.
    
    When performing rename with RENAME_WHITEOUT, dst will be replace with src, and
    meanwhile, a 'whiteout' will be create with name of src.
    
    A "whiteout" is designed to be a char
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces RENAME_WHITEOUT support but contains the vulnerability described in the root cause. Specifically: (1) The whiteout inode is created via f2fs_create_whiteout() at line 615-617, which calls __f2fs_tmpfile() that decrements i_nlink via inode_dec_link_count() at line 555. (2) The code then performs partial directory modifications: f2fs_delete_entry() at line 687 deletes the source entry, and f2fs_add_link() at line 691 attempts to add the whiteout entry. (3) Critically, if f2fs_add_link() fails at line 691, the function jumps to 'put_out_dir' at line 693, but there is NO dentry cache invalidation (no d_invalidate() or similar call) before the error handling. (4) The whiteout inode is then released via iput(whiteout) at line 696, but the VFS dentry cache still contains stale mappings pointing to the whiteout inode with already-decremented i_nlink. (5) The old_dentry's VFS cache is also not invalidated after f2fs_delete_entry() succeeds but before f2fs_add_link() fails, leaving stale mappings. The fix would require calling d_invalidate() on the affected dentries when f2fs_add_link() fails, but this is not present in this commit.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces RENAME_WHITEOUT support but contains the vulnerability described in the root cause. The vulnerable sequence is present: (1) f2fs_delete_entry(old_entry, old_page, old_dir, NULL) at line 687 deletes the source entry and decrements i_nlink; (2) f2fs_add_link(old_dentry, whiteout) at line 692 attempts to add the whiteout entry. If f2fs_add_link fails, the code jumps to 'put_out_dir' label (line 719) which calls f2fs_unlock_op(sbi) and then 'out_whiteout' label (line 726) which does iput(whiteout), but critically, there is NO dentry cache invalidation (no d_invalidate or similar call) for the old_dentry. This leaves the VFS dentry cache with stale mappings pointing to the old_inode whose i_nlink has already been decremented by f2fs_delete_entry. The vulnerability exists because the partial directory modifications (delete source, then attempt add whiteout) are not atomic, and failure to add the whiteout entry leaves the VFS cache in an inconsistent state without invalidating the stale dentry.
